title: No Verified Record Can Defend Vietnam’s Dog-Trade System
excerpt: No police seizure, court judgment, or official health alert appears here. Claims about dog farms and stolen pets need records, while biosecurity gaps demand action.
body_html:
No verified seizure, court judgment, or emergency health alert accompanies this dispatch. That absence cannot prove that no theft, poisoning, or unsafe transport occurred. It does block honest reporting of a specific victim, location, or criminal network.

Myths Need Records

“Farm-raised dogs” cannot serve as a blanket defense without traceable origin records, veterinary inspection, transport documents, and quarantine controls. “Tradition” cannot excuse stolen companion animals, illegal transport, poison use, or uninspected slaughter where those acts are documented by police or courts. None of those records appears in the material available here.

Biosecurity Has No Shortcut

Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters through bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. Handling sick animals, uninspected slaughter, and bite attacks create risk. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. After possible exposure, wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes. Seek urgent medical care for post-exposure prophylaxis, including vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once symptoms develop, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. WHO guidance explains rabies exposure and prevention.

Household exposure incidents and commercial supply chains are separate dimensions of biosecurity. One cannot be used to invent facts about the other. Both require transparent records, quarantine enforcement, and accountable institutions.

Vietnamese Communities Can Demand Proof and Protection

Vietnamese families and animal-protection leaders need a system that protects children, pets, and public health. SDE calls for complete abolition of the dog-meat trade by 2030. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action, then follow campaign updates on how that demand reaches decision-makers.
